column2: Execute emergency shutdown / egress — IC 21/43 TP HOT CAUTION LIGHT – GROUND: execute emergency shutdown/egress. Gouge p.59 #7 / p.64 #13: same procedure as FIRE light on deck.

column2: Caution (yellow); warning (red) — Gouge p.60 #26: TP HOT is a CAUTION light (yellow), not a WARNING light (red) — RTFQ.

column1: TP HOT caution light firewire threshold vs. FIRE warning light threshold:
column2: 150°C for TP HOT; 300°C for FIRE — Gouge p.37 / p.54 #123–125: FIRE and GTS FIRE = 300°C outside the container; TP HOT = 150°C.

column1: GTS FIRE warning light IN FLIGHT. Per IC 21/43, step 1 is:
column2: Engine switch – Off — IC 21/43 GTS FIRE WARNING LIGHT – IN-FLIGHT: 1. Engine switch – off. Gouge agrees (p.59 #12, p.65: 'Engine switch – Off' first).

column2: There is an overtemperature condition in the GTS compartment — Gouge p.62 (E): overtemperature in the GTS compartment (not a fire in the burner can). p.54 #124: temp outside GTS container exceeds 300°C.

column1: If the FIRE light comes on and then goes out, the gouge says this means:
column2: Firewire temperature dropped below 300°C (fire out) — or burn-through — Gouge p.3: 'if the fire light comes on then turns off = temp below 300 or burn through.' p.37: firewire must remain below 300°C for 45 sec for the light to go out. p.53 #113: check light/continuity.

column2: Throttle – off — IC 21/43: 1. Throttle – off. Gouge p.77 #36 and p.59 #11 (overspeed on start: Throttle Off, not Throttle Idle).

column1: Engine fails to light off within 15 seconds after moving the throttle to IDLE. This is a:
column2: Wet start — Quizlet EP1 #1 / gouge p.5 #1, p.62 (G); p.56 #168: wet start = FF rises normally but no EGT/RPM within 15 s of idle.

column1: RPM stagnates around 45% while EGT continues to rise during start. This is a:
column2: Hung start — Gouge p.4 / p.56 #168: hung start = RPM stuck ~45%, EGT rising.

column1: Hot start (gouge definition):
column2: FF and RPM normal, but EGT rapidly to 550°C or to 570°C for more than 10 seconds — Gouge p.56 #168. Ground start limit 550°C (570°C max for 10 s), p.37/p.56.

column1: Overspeed during engine start — first step:
column2: Throttle – off (clear engine procedure) — Gouge p.59 #11, p.65 'OVERSPEED START – THROTTLE OFF'; matches IC 21/43 Clear Engine step 1.

column2: 1,500 feet AGL and 180 KIAS — IC 21/43: If below 1,500 feet AGL and airspeed below 180 KIAS: 1. Eject. Otherwise: 2. Execute airstart. Gouge p.4, p.7 #2, p.60 #18, p.74 #10.

column2: Eject — Below 1,500 ft AGL AND below 180 KIAS → Eject (IC 21/43 ENGINE FAILURE; Quizlet EP1 #8).

column2: No — airstart is not performed for a fire — Gouge p.61 'No airstart – FIRE in FLT'; p.65 'FIRE WARNING LIGHT – DO NOT DO AIRSTART'.

column2: No — throttle idle first; airstart/emergency O2 are flameout actions — Gouge p.65: STALL – first step Throttle – Idle; do you perform airstart – NO; pull emerg O2 – NO. FLAMEOUT – you do those first.

column2: Compressor (engine) stall — Quizlet EP1 #2; gouge p.3, p.60 #17, p.61 (FF same).

column2: Execute engine failure procedure — IC 21/43 step 3. Gouge p.54 #120: locked in stall = EGT over 450 for 6 seconds after selecting idle.

column1: Per IC 21/43, after a compressor stall, if EGT responds normally you:
column2: Throttle – slowly advance to minimum for safe flight; minimize throttle movements — IC 21/43 steps 4–5.

column1: The EGT/RPM warning light illuminates at:
Per IC 21/43 ABORT, step 2 is:
column2: Speed brakes – extend — IC 21/43 ABORT: 1. Throttle – idle 2. Speed brakes – extend 3. Brakes – apply 4. Hook – down (if required) 5. Brakes – release prior to crossing the arresting gear. Older gouge p.5 #9 / Quizlet EP1 #9 'BOARDS retract' — older gouge, differs (Quizlet EP2 #25 says 'extend').

column1: Per IC 21/43 ABORT, the final step is:
column2: Brakes – release prior to crossing the arresting gear — IC 21/43 step 5. The gouge abort items stop at 'hook (1000 ft prior)'.

column1: During an aborted takeoff with NO blown tire, the anti-skid switch should be:
column2: Left ON (do not turn anti-skid off) — Gouge p.62 (C): for an aborted T/O (assuming no blown tire) DO NOT TURN ANTISKID OFF.

column1: Per IC 21/43 FIRE WARNING LIGHT on TAKEOFF, if fire is confirmed and you are unable to abort:
column2: Eject — IC 21/43: If decision is made to stop: 1. Abort. If fire is confirmed and unable to abort: 2. Eject. Gouge p.60 #19, p.66 #21, p.74 #11.

column1: Per the gouge, the first indication of a fire on takeoff is:
column2: The FIRE light — Gouge p.3 and p.47 (TRUE).

column1: Maximum abort speed is defined as the speed from which you can:
column2: Commence a stop on the remaining runway without using the overrun or arresting gear — Aero gouge p.2 #33. (Aero notes: 'Max abort 125 – not 129'.)

column1: Per IC 21/43 EMERGENCY CATAPULT FLYAWAY, steps 1 and 2 are:
column2: Throttle – MRT; maintain 24 units AOA — IC 21/43: 1. Throttle – MRT 2. Maintain 24 units AOA; if engine failed or unable to stop settle: 3. Eject. Gouge: 'throttle check full forward, 24 AOA'.

column1: Engine failure during the catapult stroke. Per IC 21/43:
column2: Eject — IC 21/43 EMERGENCY CATAPULT FLYAWAY: if engine failed or unable to stop settle – Eject. Gouge adds: if unable to eject, ditch straight ahead (p.5 #15, p.59 #6).

column1: Per the gouge, ditching configuration is:
column2: Gear up, flaps full down — Gouge p.59 #8, p.65, p.61.

column1: Launch bar warning light after a cat launch (per the gouge):
column2: Divert to a field and make a flared/minimum-descent-rate landing with the short-field arresting gear removed — Quizlet EP2 #29; gouge p.75 #20. p.72: L-BAR extended → land past arrest gear.

column1: Launch bar actuation per the gouge systems notes:
column2: Extended (lowered) by HYD 1, retracted (raised) by a mechanical spring; electrically controlled — Gouge p.3, p.54 #140 and hw correction p.60: electrically controlled, hydraulically extended, mechanically retracted. NOTE: Quizlet EP1 #14 / gouge p.5 #14 says 'mechanically extended, hydraulically retracted' — conflicts with the other gouge pages.

column1: Per IC 21/43 FIRE WARNING LIGHT IN-FLIGHT, step 1 is:
column2: Throttle – minimum for safe flight — IC 21/43 IN-FLIGHT: 1. Throttle – minimum for safe flight 2. Check for secondary indications of fire. Gouge p.60 #22 'first step is Throttle idle (min for safe flight)'.

column1: Per IC 21/43 FIRE WARNING LIGHT IN-FLIGHT, after checking for secondary indications, if fire is confirmed or flight control is lost:
column2: Eject — IC 21/43 step 3. Older gouge EP 11X p.76 #31 adds O2 pull, Throttle Off, Fuel Shutoff Pull, then eject / prepare for controlled ejection / flameout approach — older gouge, differs.

column1: Per IC 21/43 FIRE WARNING LIGHT IN-FLIGHT, if fire is NOT confirmed and control effectiveness remains:
column2: Land as soon as possible — IC 21/43 step 4. The older gouge has no 'land as soon as possible' branch.

column1: Secondary indications of an engine fire (per the gouge):
column2: Rising EGT, increased fuel flow (plus the FIRE light) — all of the above — Gouge p.65: SECONDARY INDICATIONS OF FIRE: EGT ↑, FUEL FLOW ↑, FIRE LIGHT; p.59 #13 (startup: all of the above); p.47.

column1: Cruising at 23K you get a FIRE light with secondary indications. Answer per the gouge/Quizlet (consistent with IC 21/43 'fire confirmed'):
column2: EJECT (not prepare for controlled ejection) — Quizlet EP1 #18 / gouge p.5 #18; IC 21/43: if fire confirmed – Eject.

column1: Per IC 21/43 ELECTRICAL FIRE, the immediate action is:
column2: Gen switch – off — IC 21/43 ELECTRICAL FIRE: 1. Gen switch – off. Quizlet EP2 #3 matches.

column1: Per IC 21/43 TOTAL ELECTRICAL FAILURE, the memory item is:
column2: Emergency oxygen green ring(s) – pull — IC 21/43: 1. Emergency oxygen green ring(s) – pull. Gouge EP 11X p.68/p.74 starts the same, then VMC, land as soon as practical, reset gen/batts, emergency gear, no-flap/no-slat arrested landing.

column1: Total electrical failure: load shedding is:
column2: Not a factor / not necessary — Gouge p.71 #28, p.74 #2, p.7 #26 / Quizlet EP2 #26: no load shedding (eliminates 3 of 4 answers).

column1: Total electrical failure landing plan (gouge EP 11X):
column2: No-flap/no-slat approach and arrested landing (short-field trap recommended — no NWS) — Gouge p.68 #2, p.74 #2; p.3: no emergency flaps with total electrical failure; p.51 #52: only the gear can be extended manually.

column1: With a complete electrical failure, what can still be extended manually?
column2: Landing gear only (not the flaps) — Gouge p.51 #52 (False — only the gear).

column1: First step for a GENERATOR warning light (gouge EP 11X):
column2: Confirm engine operation — Gouge p.71 #16, p.75 #15a, Quizlet EP2 #30.

column1: Generator failure indications:
column2: Master caution, tone, GEN warning light, loss of right MFD and HUD — Gouge p.3, p.52 #72. TACAN remains (p.4).

column1: To keep the left MFD powered during a generator failure:
column2: DISPLAY POWER switch – ORIDE — Gouge p.4, p.70/p.75 #15i; p.51 #58: LT MFD reverts to ADI, out after 2 minutes unless ORIDE.

column1: With a generator failure (28 VDC generator bus lost), which trim remains?
column2: Primary stabilator trim only — Gouge p.8 #35, p.76 #25, p.52 hw; p.55 #162: lose ail/rud/stby stab trim, trim indicators, HUD, RT MFD.

column1: Battery endurance after generator failure:
column2: 27 minutes on two good batteries (12 minutes on one) — Gouge p.51 #62.

column1: Overvoltage unit takes the generator offline at:
column2: 30.2 VDC — Gouge p.3, p.47 #14, p.51 #57; undervoltage unit deenergizes non-essential buses below 25 VDC.

column1: Single AC inverter failure results in:
column2: AC INV caution light, tone, and loss of non-essential AC (VOR/ILS/MB/RADALT) — Gouge p.3, p.31 #20, p.52 #64, #69; with one inverter failed you still have TACAN azimuth (p.52 #67).

column1: With both inverters failed, what navigation is left?
column2: PAR approaches only — Gouge p.52 #68; p.69: DUAL FAIL → TCN azimuth lost.

column1: AC INV caution light (per gouge/Quizlet EP2 #32):
column2: Reset number 1 and 2 inverters — Gouge p.8 #32.

column1: Approach idle function with total electrical failure:
column2: Engages (normally held open magnetically) — Gouge p.55 #163 (True).

column1: CAUG (control augmentation) caution light in flight — you lose:
column2: ARI, SBI, yaw damper, and rudder trim — Gouge p.4, p.66 #32, p.71 #19, p.75 #18; Quizlet EP2 #15.

column1: The CONTR AUG caution light illuminates when:
column2: The system is degraded, a BIT test is in progress, or the paddle switch has been depressed — Gouge p.41; p.61 hw 'CAUG Illum – FAILURE, BIT TEST, PADDLE OFF'.

column1: CAUG BIT requirements:
column2: Weight on wheels, less than 80 knots, flaps/slats up — Gouge p.41, p.52 #86, p.71 #24.

column1: Trim-failure exam question answer (gouge):
column2: ADI indicates 2 degrees nose up — Gouge p.64 #3, p.68 #3. Related: a 2° pitch change during speed brake extension/retraction is normal with the SBI (p.67, p.71 #27).

column1: Speed brakes: may not fully extend above ___; blowback occurs above ___.
SLATS caution light coming into the break:
column2: Slow to and maintain below 200 KIAS; land as soon as practical — Gouge p.64 #5, p.71 #30, p.74 #4, p.76 #28; Quizlet EP2 #4.

column1: SLATS caution light illuminates when:
column2: Slats not in selected position, split slats, or slats selected/extended above 217 knots — Gouge p.42, p.49 #38, p.71 #29.

column1: Per IC 21/43 ASYMMETRIC FLAPS/SLATS (uncommanded roll/yaw during flap/slat transition):
column2: FLAPS/SLATS lever – Return to previous setting — IC 21/43. Gouge p.7 #7 / Quizlet EP2 #7: return flaps to previous position. p.4: rapid roll during flap/slat transition = split flap/slat.

column1: Why may the flap position light not show a split flap?
column2: It is connected to the left flap only — Gouge p.35.

column1: HYD 1 or HYD 2 failure — first consideration (gouge):
column2: Reduce airspeed below 300 KIAS / 0.6 Mach — Quizlet EP1 #16 / gouge p.5 #16.

column1: With a HYD 2 failure you should monitor:
column2: HYD 1 pressure gauge (not the accumulator) — Gouge p.59 #15, p.65; Quizlet EP1 #21.

column1: With a HYD 2 pressure failure, the RAT maintains HYD 2 pressure at:
column2: 2,500–3,000 psi — Quizlet EP1 #4; gouge p.5 #4, p.62 (A), p.57.

column1: The RAT deploys when HYD 2 falls below ___ psi; HYD 2 reset requires ___ psi.
column2: 1,500 psi; 1,800 psi — Gouge p.48, p.49 #27/#30, p.57. HYD 2 caution light on at 1,660 ± 110, out at 2,000 psi.

column1: HYD 1 failure — what is still available for landing?
column2: Emergency gear extension, emergency flaps, and an arrested landing (all of the above) — Gouge p.59 #14, p.65.

column1: HYD 1 below 1,500 psi — general services lost include:
column2: Normal gear, normal flaps/slats, normal brakes, NWS, L-bar extension, speed brakes, hook retract — Gouge p.49 #37 (priority valve isolates flight controls at 1,500 psi, p.40/p.57).

column1: Effect of a HYD 1 failure on the tailhook:
column2: It can be lowered (gravity/snubber) but not raised — Gouge p.51 #53, p.54 #138, p.3.

column1: HYD 1 and HYD 2 failed, RAT working, but the aircraft is 'uncontrollable':
column2: Eject — Gouge p.59 #1, p.64 #6 — key word 'uncontrollable'.

column1: The wheel brake/emergency flap accumulator provides:
column2: 10 brake applications and emergency flap extension (no slats); flaps cut off at 2,200 psi — Gouge p.49 #31–32, p.57, p.41 (≤2,200 psi emergency flap lever has no effect).

column1: Per IC 21/43 BRAKE FAILURE – ASHORE/SKID, if flyaway airspeed is NOT available, step 2 is:
column2: Throttle – idle — IC 21/43: 1. Go around (if flyaway airspeed available). Otherwise: 2. Throttle – idle 3. Brakes – release 4. Anti-skid switch – off 5. Brakes – apply gradually 6. Hook – down 7. Parking brake handle – pull. Older gouge EP 11X p.68 #5 omits throttle idle and adds 'Throttle – OFF (if departing rwy)' — older gouge, differs.

column1: Per IC 21/43 BRAKE FAILURE – ASHORE/SKID, if brakes are still unavailable after applying gradually:
column2: Hook – down (if required); Parking brake handle – pull (if required) — IC 21/43 steps 6–7. The older gouge has no parking-brake step.

column1: Per IC 21/43 BRAKE FAILURE – AFLOAT:
column2: Throttle – idle; Parking brake handle – pull; Hook – down; Transmit — IC 21/43. Not covered by the gouge (only a topic title on p.69).

column1: Per IC 21/43 LOSS OF DIRECTIONAL CONTROL, if NWS failure is suspected:
column2: Paddle switch – press — IC 21/43 step 6. The gouge only says 'use differential braking' (p.5 #5, p.59 #10) — older gouge, differs.

column1: Per IC 21/43 LOSS OF DIRECTIONAL CONTROL, if a blown tire is suspected (no flyaway airspeed):
column2: Brakes – release; Anti-skid switch – off; Brakes – apply gradually — IC 21/43 steps 3–5. Gouge: rudder as required to counter swerve, anti-skid off prior to braking (p.60 #21, p.66 #23, p.76 #21).

column1: If aborting with a blown tire, set the ANTI-SKID switch ON — true or false?
column2: False — anti-skid OFF — Quizlet EP1 #6; IC 21/43 blown tire: anti-skid switch – off.

column1: Blown tire on takeoff, continuing the takeoff (gouge EP 11X):
column2: Rudder as required; do NOT reposition gear and flaps; monitor engine instruments; execute landing with blown tire procedure — Gouge p.70 #11.

column1: Landing with a single blown tire and no arresting gear (gouge):
column2: Flared landing with flaps ½ — Gouge p.73 #31, p.76 #22; Quizlet EP2 #20.

column1: Landing with dual blown tires and no arresting gear available (gouge):
column2: Consider a gear-up landing or controlled ejection — Gouge p.73 #32, p.67.

column1: Short-field arrestment touchdown point when directional control is IN question:
column2: At or 50 ft prior to the gear — Gouge p.73 #33, p.74 #3, p.7 #6; normal short-field arrestment: 500 ft prior.

column1: Long-field arrestment (gouge 'for test only'):
column2: Hook down 1,000 ft prior; maintain directional control; release brakes as you cross the cable — Gouge p.71 #26.

column1: NWS AUG goes on during taxi. You should:
column2: Momentarily press the NWS button — Quizlet EP1 #25 / gouge p.6 #25.

column1: Emergency (EMERG) gear extension effect on nosewheel steering:
column2: NWS is disabled (no NWS) — Gouge p.3, p.69.

column1: Anti-skid OFF situations (gouge '5 times'):
column2: After HYD 1 failure, before setting the parking brake after shutdown, carrier landings, SKID caution light, blown tire — Gouge p.3, p.35, p.54 #139.

column1: HOOK warning light meaning:
column2: Hook position does not agree with the handle — Gouge p.71 #17 (hw correction), p.44; Quizlet EP2 #33.

column1: Light in the landing gear handle:
column2: Gear in transit or not in the commanded position — Gouge p.71 #18/#25, p.75 #17, p.76 #23.

column1: Per IC 21/43 SMOKE OR FUMES IN COCKPIT, step 1 is:
column2: Mask – on/tight — IC 21/43: 1. Mask – on/tight 2. Initiate controlled descent to below 18,000 feet MSL 3. Air Flow Knob – Off. Older gouge (p.70 #12, p.75 #13) has no mask step — older gouge, differs.

column1: Per IC 21/43 SMOKE OR FUMES, initiate a controlled descent to below:
column2: 18,000 feet MSL — IC 21/43 step 2. Older gouge / Quizlet EP2 #5: 'descend below 25K' — older gouge, differs.

column1: Per IC 21/43 SMOKE OR FUMES, if unable to clear smoke or unable to see, the steps are:
column2: Airspeed – reduce; warn other occupant/secure loose items; Seat – lower; MDC Firing Handle – pull — IC 21/43 steps 4–7. Older gouge adds 'Visor – Down' and 'Land as soon as possible'.

column1: Per IC 21/43 RAPID DECOMPRESSION:
column2: Emergency oxygen green ring(s) – pull; OBOGS flow selector(s) – off; descend below 10,000 feet cabin altitude — IC 21/43 (same three steps as ADVERSE PHYSIOLOGICAL SYMPTOMS).

column1: Per IC 21/43 ADVERSE PHYSIOLOGICAL SYMPTOMS, the procedure applies if above:
column2: 10,000 feet cabin altitude — IC 21/43: If above 10,000 feet cabin altitude: 1. green ring(s) pull 2. OBOGS flow selector(s) off 3. descend below 10,000 ft cabin altitude. Gouge/Quizlet EP2 #1: descend below 10,000 ft cabin alt with an OBOGS failure.

column1: Per IC 21/43 OXYGEN WARNING LIGHT (in flight), step 1 is:
column2: Throttle – Set minimum 80% rpm — IC 21/43: 1. Throttle – set minimum 80% rpm 2. Execute Adverse Physiological Symptoms (as required). Older gouge/Quizlet EP2 #8: 'OBOGS/ANTI-G switch off', descend below 10,000 cabin alt — older gouge, differs.

column1: OXYGEN warning light causes (gouge systems notes):
column2: O2 concentration below 95%, overheat above 250°F, or OXYGEN switch off — Gouge p.53 #106, p.44, p.51 hw (OBOGS still works just below 95%).

column1: CABIN ALT warning light procedure per the gouge (not on the IC 21/43 immediate-action list):
column2: OBOGS – on and mask tight; reduce AOA; Air Flow knob – off then on; if light remains on, descend below 25,000 ft MSL; land as soon as practical — Gouge p.68 #1, p.74 #1, p.64 #1. Not one of the 22 IC 21/43 items — don't confuse 25,000 ft with the 10,000 ft cabin altitude of RAPID DECOMPRESSION.

column1: CABIN ALT warning light illuminates at a cabin altitude above:
Canopy loss (gouge):
column2: Descend to 10,000 ft or minimum safe altitude and less than 200 KIAS — Gouge p.64 #15, p.68 #6, p.74 #8.

column1: CANOPY caution light in flight (gouge/Quizlet EP2 #21):
column2: Airspeed below 200 knots — Gouge p.7 #21. CANOPY light + tone with canopy unlocked and power above 95% (p.4, p.53).

column1: Per IC 21/43 OIL PRESS WARNING LIGHT, step 1 is:
column2: Throttle – Set and maintain 78 to 87% rpm — IC 21/43: 1. Throttle – set and maintain 78 to 87% rpm 2. Minimize throttle movements. Older gouge: 'min for safe flight' (p.59 #5) or 'idle' (p.64 #10) — older gouge, differs.

column1: ECA 2 caution light limits (gouge/Quizlet EP1 #7):
column2: Do not exceed 90% above 20K MSL, 95% below 20K MSL, 600°C EGT; land as soon as practical — Gouge p.5 #7, p.60 #24, p.65, p.66 #33.

column1: ACCEL caution light during descent passing 7,000 ft MSL:
column2: Expect slower engine acceleration during the approach — Quizlet EP1 #3; gouge p.5 #3. p.54 #115: steam ingestion valve stuck open or initial shot-of-fuel solenoid not in commanded position.

column1: LP PUMP caution light in flight:
column2: Avoid abrupt throttle movements and set minimum for flight — Quizlet EP1 #10; gouge p.5 #10. Illuminates below 35 psi (p.37, p.61).

column1: After the F PRESS light illuminates and you check the engine switch on, you should:
column2: Avoid negative G maneuvers — Quizlet EP1 #17; gouge p.5 #17. F PRESS also illuminates 30 s after a GEN failure (boost pumps stop) (p.39, p.61).

column1: MFD failure indications (gouge):
column2: Blank or blinking screen, stuck pushbutton, wrong/invalid info — Gouge p.68 #4, p.74 #6, p.30; Quizlet EP2 #11.

column1: Multiple MFD failures — corrective action:
column2: Display Power switch – momentarily to RESET — Gouge p.76 #27, p.47 #10 (single MFD: turn it off); Quizlet EP2 #22.

column1: DEU failure leaves you with which approach?
column2: PAR (or visual) only — Gouge p.52 #88, p.55 #146, p.30, p.4.

column1: Pitot-static failure question — the instrument that still works:
column2: Standby VSI — Gouge p.8 #27, p.64 #16; Quizlet EP2 #27. Complete pitot-static failure: lose mach/airspeed and barometric altitude, NOT vertical velocity (p.14).

column1: Barometric altimeter failure (gouge):
column2: Check pitot heat; use RADALT below 5,000 ft AGL; use cabin altimeter if unpressurized — Gouge p.7 #12, p.76 #24; Quizlet EP2 #12.

column1: Per IC 21/43 DEPARTURE/SPIN PROCEDURE, steps 1–3 are:
column2: Controls – neutralize/forcibly center rudder pedals; Speed brakes – retract; Throttle – idle — IC 21/43 steps 1–4 (4. check altitude, AOA, airspeed, and turn needle).

column1: Upright spin recovery per IC 21/43 (AOA above 28 units):
column2: Rudder – full opposite turn needle; lateral stick – full WITH turn needle; longitudinal stick – neutralize — IC 21/43 steps 8–10. Gouge p.25: Aileron full WITH turn needle for upright spins; p.20 #45: aileron positions reversed upright vs inverted.

column1: Inverted spin recovery per IC 21/43 (AOA pegged at 0 units):
column2: Rudder – full opposite turn needle; lateral stick – full opposite turn needle; longitudinal stick – neutralize — IC 21/43 steps 5–7. Gouge p.25: Aileron full OPPOSITE turn needle for inverted spins.

column1: Inverted spin characteristics (gouge):
column2: 0 units indicated AOA, negative G, turn needle in direction of spin — Gouge p.2 #40, p.20 #44, p.25.

column1: Per IC 21/43, if out of control passing through ___ AGL: Eject.
column2: 10,000 feet — IC 21/43 DEPARTURE/SPIN step 13.

column1: Per IC 21/43 DEPARTURE/SPIN, neutralize lateral stick when recovery is indicated or airspeed increases through:
column2: 160 KIAS — IC 21/43 step 11; then 12. Rudder pedals – smoothly center.

column1: Midair with your wingman — per the gouge, the right answer is:
column2: Have someone else (not the aircraft you hit) give you a visual inspection; don't have the wingman join up — Gouge p.59 #4, p.64 #9, p.65.

column1: In ejection situations the gouge says to:
column2: Trade airspeed for altitude — Gouge p.60 #27, p.65.

column1: Engine EGT limits (gouge): max at idle / ground start / airstart:
column2: 450°C / 550°C (570°C for 10 s) / 600°C (650°C for 10 s) — Gouge p.37, p.56. MRT 610°C (30 min/hr); transient 645°C (<20 s).

column1: HYD 1 / HYD 2 normal pressure and pump output?
column2: 3000 psi; HYD 1 EDP 9.6 gpm, HYD 2 EDP 6 gpm [gouge p.57]

column1: Flight-control accumulator nitrogen precharge?
Wheel brake/emergency flap accumulator nitrogen preload?
HYD 1 priority valve: closes (isolating flight controls from general services) at ___ psi and reopens at ___ psi?
column2: Closes at 1500 psi; reopens at 1600 psi [gouge p.40, p.57]

column1: Brake accumulator drops below ___ psi → emergency flap actuation removed to isolate emergency brakes?
HYD 1 PRESS caution light on / off?
column2: On below 1660 ± 110 psi (post-AFC 244); off at 2000 psi (p.54 #131; p.57 shows 725 ± 50 'light out', hand-annotated) [gouge p.33, p.49 #28, p.54 #131, p.57]

column1: HYD 2 PRESS caution light on / off?
column2: On below 1660 ± 110 psi; off above 2000 psi [gouge p.40, p.48, p.49 #26]

column1: RAT retracts as HYD 2 pressure is lost at?
column2: 700 psi (aerodynamic load permitting) [gouge p.40, p.57]

column1: RAT governor speed?
column2: 7300 rpm [gouge p.57]

column1: HYD 2 bypass valve: energized open below ___ N2; HYD 2 RESET usable above ___ N2?
column2: Below 42% N2 open; HYD 2 RESET above 45% N2 [gouge p.33, p.40, p.49 #33, p.57]

column1: Three requirements for the HYD FAIL warning light?
column2: HYD 1 < 600 ± 50 psi, HYD 2 < 1660 ± 110 psi, and emergency system < 600 ± 50 psi [gouge p.40, p.57]

column1: HYD FAIL illuminates if RAT pressure drops below?
column2: 600 ± 100 psi [gouge p.33]

column1: Hand pump maximum pressure?
column2: 2800 psi [?] (scan) [gouge p.33]

column1: Emergency flap extension drives flaps to?
column2: Full down regardless of flap lever (if sufficient pressure) [gouge p.41]

column1: If HYD 1 fails with slats fully extended, will airloads drive them retracted?
column2: No (FALSE) [gouge p.41]

column1: Indication of an operable RAT?
column2: HYD 2 fluctuating between 2500–3000 psi [gouge p.54 #128]

column1: If HYD 2 and the RAT fail, effect on the total HYD system?
column2: None — HYD 1 still operates everything normally [gouge p.54 #129]

column1: If HYD 2 is leaking, will the RAT do the job?
column2: No [gouge p.54 #130]

column1: Slow loss of HYD 2 pressure — are general services lost?
column2: No (general services are on HYD 1) [gouge p.3]

column1: First indication of a slow HYD 1 pressure loss (pre-AFC 244)?
column2: 1500 psi — loss of general services (no light before AFC 244) [gouge p.49 #29]

column1: During ACM: HYD caution, RAT caution, then HYD light extinguishes — answer?
column2: Reset HYD 2 (correct, but not the first thing to do) [gouge p.6 #23 / Quizlet EP1 #23]

column1: Max N2 at MRT / transient / continuous?
Manual fuel control N2 limits?
column2: ≤95% N2 below 20,000 ft; ≤90% N2 above 20,000 ft (prevents N1 overspeed) [gouge p.37]

column1: Approach idle minimum rpm?
column2: 72% (gear down, no weight on wheels) [gouge p.37, p.52 #76]

column1: Max EGT at MRT and time limit?
column2: 610°C; 30 min per flight hour [gouge p.34, p.37, p.56]

column1: Max transient EGT?
column2: 645°C, time restricted to < 20 sec [gouge p.37, p.56]

column1: Max continuous EGT?
column2: 550°C (time unrestricted) [gouge p.37, p.56]

column1: Max EGT overshoot during airstart / ground start?
column2: 50°C above 600°C (10 s max) / 20°C above 550°C (10 s max) [gouge p.37]

column1: Idle limits?
Start limits?
column2: FF 300–400; EGT 550 (570 for 10 s); RPM 52 ± 2 within 30 s of idle [gouge p.56 #175]

column1: Minimum N2 for engine start / airstart?
GTS start attempt intervals?
column2: 3 min between attempts; 30 min after three attempts [gouge p.37]

column1: GTS advisory light time limits?
column2: 20 s on the ground (sea level); 28 s in flight (airstarts) [gouge p.34, p.37]

column1: READY light?

column2: Insufficient differential pressure across a boost pump, or fuel tank air pressure below 3 psi; also 30 s after GEN failure [gouge p.39]

column2: Malfunction detected, prolonged full dump > 2 s, or no wheel spin 3 s after WOW (reverts to normal braking) [gouge p.43, p.35]

column1: PARKING BRAKE caution light?
column2: Parking brake set and throttle advanced beyond ~60–70% (N2 above 70%) [gouge p.43, p.52]

column1: Red L BAR light?

column1: With a launch bar retraction failure, raising the gear is not possible?

column1: Paddle switch?
column2: Disengages NWS and control augmentation [gouge p.35, p.43, p.49 #39]

column1: Reset NWS and CAUG?

column2: Hold reset ~5 s / reset momentarily — don't hold in reset [gouge p.34, p.67]

column1: Undervoltage indications?
column2: GEN warning light, master caution; undervoltage unit deenergizes non-essential buses below 25 VDC [gouge p.47, p.51]

column1: Undervoltage sensing unit failed (GEN normal) — CWS lights?
column2: None [gouge p.31]

column1: With GEN failure: TACAN? GINA? ADI turn indicator?
column2: TACAN yes; GINA yes; ADI turn indicator no [gouge p.4, p.55 #153, p.45]

column2: Mach/airspeed and barometric altitude — NOT vertical velocity [gouge p.14]

column1: ADI display failure?
column2: Use the standby attitude indicator [gouge p.31, p.15]

column1: Nose-high / nose-low unusual attitude partial panel?

column1: AOA indication failure?
column2: Use the airspeed indicator; AOA off flag → can't use indexer [gouge p.15, p.31]

column1: Total GINA failure indications?
column2: Blanking of attitude and heading on ADI, HSI, and HUD [gouge p.15]

column1: ATC reports loss of altitude information?
column2: IFF failure [gouge p.32]

column1: Impending stall best indications?
column2: Rudder shakers and tone (artificial stall warning 21.5 units) [gouge p.4, p.1]

column1: Spin rates of descent?

column1: −60° inverted spin airspeed?

column1: Increase altitude for better?
column2: Radio reception [gouge p.60 #31]

column1: Structural damage may require you to?
column2: Blow the canopy [gouge p.60 #32]

column1: NWS AUG failure — arrestment touchdown point?
column2: Touch down just before (50 ft) the arresting gear [gouge p.72]

column2: Gravity, assisted by snubber/pneumatic [gouge p.3, p.54 #138]
